questions.problem: Find the horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=\frac{2x+5}{2{x}^{3}+2x+6}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y={lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{3}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{2x+5}{2{x}^{3}+2x+6} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{2x}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{5}{{x}^{3}})}{(\frac{2{x}^{3}}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{2x}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{6}{{x}^{3}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{2}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{5}{{x}^{3}})}{(2+\frac{2}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{6}{{x}^{3}})} \\  & =\frac{0+0}{2+0+0} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the horizontal asymptote of $f(x)$ is $y=0.$

questions.problem: Given that the horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=\frac{5{x}^{2}-6}{c{x}^{2}+32x+8}$ is $y=\frac{1}{4},$ find the value of $c.$
questions.worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y={lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{2}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{5{x}^{2}-6}{c{x}^{2}+32x+8} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{5{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{6}{{x}^{2}})}{(\frac{c{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{32x}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{8}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(5-\frac{6}{{x}^{2}})}{(c+\frac{32}{x}+\frac{8}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & =\frac{5-0}{c+0+0} \\  & =\frac{5}{c}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{c} & =\frac{1}{4} \\ c & =20.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the horizontal asymptote of $y=f(x)$ where $f(x)=\frac{11{x}^{5}-9{x}^{6}}{2{x}^{5}-1}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y={lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{5}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{11{x}^{5}-9{x}^{6}}{2{x}^{5}-1} \\  & {lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{11{x}^{5}}{{x}^{5}}-\frac{9{x}^{6}}{{x}^{5}})}{(\frac{2{x}^{5}}{{x}^{5}}-\frac{1}{{x}^{5}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(11-9x)}{(2-\frac{1}{{x}^{5}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{11-9x}{2-0} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{lim}_{x\to \infty }(11-9x) \\  & =-\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

 

The limit does not come out to a finite number. Therefore, there is no horizontal asymptote.

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,\frac{8{x}^{6}+5}{2{x}^{5}-7x} & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,\frac{(\frac{8{x}^{6}}{{x}^{5}}+\frac{5}{{x}^{5}})}{(\frac{2{x}^{5}}{{x}^{5}}-\frac{7x}{{x}^{5}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,\frac{(8x+\frac{5}{{x}^{5}})}{(2-\frac{7}{{x}^{4}})} \\  & =\frac{8x+0}{2-0} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,4x \\  & =\infty .\end{aligned}
